claim: Cytokinesis nodes are assemblies of stoichiometric ratios of proteins associated with the plasma membrane.
source: Cytokinesis nodes are assemblies of stoichiometric ratios of proteins associated with the plasma membrane, which serve as precursors for the contractile ring during cytokinesis by fission yeast.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work (Vavylonis et al., 2008) in the introduction.

claim: Cytokinesis nodes serve as precursors for the contractile ring during cytokinesis by fission yeast.
source: Cytokinesis nodes are assemblies of stoichiometric ratios of proteins associated with the plasma membrane, which serve as precursors for the contractile ring during cytokinesis by fission yeast.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to previous work (Vavylonis et al., 2008) in the introduction.

claim: Wild-type fission yeast cells have about 190 single cytokinesis nodes early in mitosis.
source: The ratio of the total Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in the broad band of cytokinesis nodes to the average fluorescence of a single node gives about 190 single cytokinesis nodes in wild-type fission yeast cells early in mitosis.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on Airyscan microscopy measurements and calculations described in the Results section.

claim: Most, but not all cytokinesis nodes condense into a contractile ring.
source: Most, but not all of these nodes condense into a contractile ring.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2E showing about 85% of Blt1 in nodes is incorporated into contractile rings.

claim: The number of cytokinesis nodes scales with cell size in four strains tested.
source: The number of cytokinesis nodes scales with cell size in four strains tested, although large diameter rga4Δ mutant cells form somewhat fewer cytokinesis nodes than expected from the overall trend.
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 3H, I with linear regression analysis showing significant correlation.

claim: Large diameter rga4Δ mutant cells form somewhat fewer cytokinesis nodes than expected from the overall trend.
source: The number of cytokinesis nodes scales with cell size in four strains tested, although large diameter rga4Δ mutant cells form somewhat fewer cytokinesis nodes than expected from the overall trend.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3H where rga4Δ cells deviate from the linear trend.

claim: The Pom1 kinase restricts cytokinesis nodes from the ends of cells.
source: The Pom1 kinase restricts cytokinesis nodes from the ends of cells, but the surface density of Pom1 on the plasma membrane around the equators of cells is similar with a wide range of node numbers, so Pom1 does not control cytokinesis node number.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4C showing constant Pom1 intensity across different cell sizes.

claim: The surface density of Pom1 on the plasma membrane around the equators of cells is similar with a wide range of node numbers.
source: The Pom1 kinase restricts cytokinesis nodes from the ends of cells, but the surface density of Pom1 on the plasma membrane around the equators of cells is similar with a wide range of node numbers, so Pom1 does not control cytokinesis node number.
evidence: This is a primary finding shown in Figure 4C with linear regression showing no significant correlation.

claim: Pom1 does not control cytokinesis node number through its local concentration at the equator.
source: The Pom1 kinase restricts cytokinesis nodes from the ends of cells, but the surface density of Pom1 on the plasma membrane around the equators of cells is similar with a wide range of node numbers, so Pom1 does not control cytokinesis node number.
evidence: This is concluded from the data in Figure 4C, D showing no correlation between local Pom1 concentration and node number.

claim: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes increase above a baseline of about 190 when the concentrations of either kinase Pom1 or kinase Cdr2 are varied with the nmt1 promoter.
source: However, when the concentrations of either kinase Pom1 or kinase Cdr2 were varied with the nmt1 promoter, the numbers of cytokinesis nodes increased above a baseline of about ~190 with the total cellular concentration of either kinase.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 5G and 6E showing increased node numbers with increased kinase expression.

claim: Cytokinesis nodes form from two distinct types of interphase nodes.
source: In fission yeast, cytokinesis nodes form from two distinct types of interphase nodes (Akamatsu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Akamatsu et al., 2014.

claim: Type 1 nodes contain kinases Cdr1 and Cdr2.
source: At the end of cytokinesis, type 1 nodes containing kinases Cdr1 and Cdr2 appear in a broad band around the middle of the daughter cells as SIN (septation initiation network) activity drops (Pu et al., 2015) and remain stationary throughout the interphase (Akamatsu et al., 2014; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Morrell et al., 2004; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Type 1 nodes remain stationary throughout interphase.
source: At the end of cytokinesis, type 1 nodes containing kinases Cdr1 and Cdr2 appear in a broad band around the middle of the daughter cells as SIN (septation initiation network) activity drops (Pu et al., 2015) and remain stationary throughout the interphase (Akamatsu et al., 2014; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Morrell et al., 2004; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Type 2 nodes contain the proteins Blt1p, Klp8p, Gef2p, and Nod1p.
source: Type 2 nodes containing the proteins Blt1p, Klp8p, Gef2p, and Nod1p (Jourdain et al., 2013; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Morrell et al., 2004; Moseley et al., 2009; Ye et al., 2012) originate from the constricting contractile ring from the previous cell cycle and diffuse along the plasma membrane from the new ends of the daughter cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Type 2 nodes originate from the constricting contractile ring from the previous cell cycle and diffuse along the plasma membrane from the new ends of the daughter cells.
source: Type 2 nodes containing the proteins Blt1p, Klp8p, Gef2p, and Nod1p (Jourdain et al., 2013; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Morrell et al., 2004; Moseley et al., 2009; Ye et al., 2012) originate from the constricting contractile ring from the previous cell cycle and diffuse along the plasma membrane from the new ends of the daughter cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: During the G2 phase of the cell cycle, type 1 nodes capture diffusing type 2 nodes to form cytokinesis nodes.
source: During the G2 phase of the cell cycle, type 1 nodes capture diffusing type 2 nodes to form cytokinesis nodes (Akamatsu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Akamatsu et al., 2014.

claim: During 10 min prior to spindle pole body (SPB) separation, cytokinesis nodes mature by sequentially accumulating stoichiometric ratios of myosin-II (Myo2 heavy chain and two light chains), IQGAP Rng2p, and F-BAR protein Cdc15p.
source: During 10 min prior to spindle pole body (SPB) separation, cytokinesis nodes mature by sequentially accumulating stoichiometric ratios of myosin-II (Myo2 heavy chain and two light chains), IQGAP Rng2p, and F-BAR protein Cdc15p (Vavylonis et al., 2008; Wu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: At the time of SPB separation, smaller numbers of formin Cdc12p join each node, where they nucleate and elongate actin filaments.
source: At the time of SPB separation, smaller numbers of formin Cdc12p join each node, where they nucleate and elongate actin filaments (Laporte et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Interactions between actin filaments from one node and myosin-II in adjacent nodes pull the nodes together into a contractile ring.
source: Interactions between actin filaments from one node and myosin-II in adjacent nodes pull the nodes together into a contractile ring (Vavylonis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Vavylonis et al., 2008.

claim: 10–12 min after SPB separation, high SIN activity disperses the Cdr2p-mEGFP from the cytokinesis nodes into the cytoplasm.
source: Interestingly, 10–12 min after SPB separation, high SIN activity disperses the Cdr2p-mEGFP from the cytokinesis nodes into the cytoplasm (Akamatsu et al., 2014; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Morrell et al., 2004; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Interphase cells grow linearly at their tips.
source: Interphase cells grow linearly at their tips (Fantes and Nurse, 1977; Moreno et al., 1989) until they reach a threshold size of twice the initial cell length (Gu and Oliferenko, 2019; Neumann and Nurse, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Interphase cells grow until they reach a threshold size of twice the initial cell length.
source: Interphase cells grow linearly at their tips (Fantes and Nurse, 1977; Moreno et al., 1989) until they reach a threshold size of twice the initial cell length (Gu and Oliferenko, 2019; Neumann and Nurse, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: During the growth period, the interphase node components double in number.
source: During this period, the interphase node components also double in number (Allard et al., 2018; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Interphase nodes are thought to sense the cell surface area to control cell size at the time of division.
source: Interphase nodes are thought to sense the cell surface area to control cell size at the time of division (Facchetti et al., 2019a; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The fluorescence from node markers ranges from tiny dim spots to much larger and brighter particles both during interphase and mitosis.
source: Rather than appearing as a uniform population of spots, the fluorescence from node markers ranges from tiny dim spots to much larger and brighter particles both during interphase (Moseley et al., 2009) and mitosis (Vavylonis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Histograms of fluorescence intensity per node show that small, dim nodes predominate.
source: Histograms of fluorescence intensity per node show that small, dim nodes predominate, although the eye of the observer is drawn to larger, more intense spots (Akamatsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Akamatsu et al., 2017.

claim: Single-molecule localization super-resolution microscopy (SMLM) by Laplante et al., 2016 explained the heterogeneity of node intensities and sizes.
source: Single-molecule localization super-resolution microscopy (SMLM) by Laplante et al., 2016 explained the heterogeneity of node intensities and sizes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: The 35 nm resolution of SMLM revealed that cytokinesis nodes in live cells are much smaller (<100 nm) than their diffraction-limited images in confocal micrographs.
source: The 35 nm resolution of this method revealed that cytokinesis nodes in live cells are much smaller (<100 nm) than their diffraction-limited images in confocal micrographs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to the SMLM method by Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: Cytokinesis nodes are uniform in size and contain stoichiometric ratios of proteins, each with a distinct spatial distribution within the node.
source: These particles are uniform in size and contain stoichiometric ratios of proteins, each with a distinct spatial distribution within the node.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to findings from SMLM by Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: Some tiny, single nodes are so close together that they have twice or three times the numbers of localizations of single nodes, accounting for the variation in node intensity in confocal micrographs.
source: Some of these tiny, single nodes are so close together that they have twice or three times the numbers of localizations of single nodes, accounting for the variation in node intensity in confocal micrographs.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to findings from SMLM by Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: Blurring the super-resolution images of nodes with the point spread function of a confocal microscope reproduced the heterogeneous mixtures of sizes and intensities.
source: Blurring the super-resolution images of nodes with the point spread function of a confocal microscope reproduced the heterogeneous mixtures of sizes and intensities.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction referring to findings from SMLM by Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: SMLM showed that the two types of interphase nodes are also tiny structures that tend to form clusters with twice or three times the number of localizations of single nodes.
source: SMLM showed that the two types of interphase nodes are also tiny structures that tend to form clusters with twice or three times the number of localizations of single nodes (Akamatsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Akamatsu et al., 2017.

claim: Vavylonis et al., 2008 counted 63 ± 10 cytokinesis nodes tagged with Rlc1-3GFP in the broad bands of wild-type cells in 3D reconstructions of z-series acquired by spinning disk confocal microscopy.
source: Vavylonis et al., 2008 counted 63 ± 10 cytokinesis nodes tagged with Rlc1-3GFP in the broad bands of wild-type cells in 3D reconstructions of z-series acquired by spinning disk confocal microscopy.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Vavylonis et al., 2008.

claim: Deng and Moseley, 2013 applied deconvolution to images obtained in wide-field microscopy and counted 52–106 interphase nodes tagged with Cdr2-mCherry.
source: Deng and Moseley, 2013 applied deconvolution to images obtained in wide-field microscopy and counted 52–106 interphase nodes tagged with Cdr2-mCherry.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Deng and Moseley, 2013.

claim: Pan et al., 2014 used the Find Maxima macro function in ImageJ to find pixels with maximum intensity in maximum projection images and counted <50 interphase nodes.
source: Pan et al., 2014 used the Find Maxima macro function in ImageJ to find pixels with maximum intensity in maximum projection images and counted <50 interphase nodes and noted that the number scaled with cell length.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Pan et al., 2014.

claim: Pan et al., 2014 noted that the number of interphase nodes scaled with cell length.
source: Pan et al., 2014 used the Find Maxima macro function in ImageJ to find pixels with maximum intensity in maximum projection images and counted <50 interphase nodes and noted that the number scaled with cell length.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Pan et al., 2014.

claim: Allard et al., 2018 used the superior (140 nm) resolution of Airyscan microscopy and an automated particle tracking plugin to count ~50 nodes tagged with Cdr2-mEGFP during interphase.
source: Allard et al., 2018 used the superior (140 nm) resolution of Airyscan microscopy and an automated particle tracking plugin to count ~50 nodes tagged with Cdr2-mEGFP during interphase.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Allard et al., 2018.

claim: The algorithm used in the plugin by Allard et al., 2018 was designed to find only local intensity maxima and did not count the dim nodes with low intensities.
source: However, the algorithm used in the plugin was designed to find only local intensity maxima and did not count the dim nodes with low intensities.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of the method used by Allard et al., 2018.

claim: Laplante et al., 2016 estimated the number of cytokinesis nodes in fission yeast broad bands by measuring the local density of nodes in a 400-nm optical section and extrapolating this density around the equator, giving ~140 total nodes for five different tagged proteins.
source: One approach was to measure the local density of nodes in a 400-nm optical section from the top or bottom of the cell and then extrapolate this density around the equator, giving ~140 total nodes for five different tagged proteins (Mid1, Rlc1, Cdc15, Myo2, and Rng2).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: Laplante et al., 2016 blurred SMLM images with the point spread function to simulate a confocal image, resulting in about half the single nodes being blurred together, so the 65 nodes counted by Vavylonis et al., 2008 represented roughly 130 single nodes.
source: The second method was to blur the SMLM images with the point spread function to simulate a confocal image. This resulted in about half the single nodes being blurred together, so the 65 nodes counted by Vavylonis et al., 2008 represented roughly 130 single nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: Blt1 is found in interphase nodes, cytokinesis nodes, and contractile rings.
source: Blt1 is the only protein known to persist in nodes throughout the cell cycle, so it is found in interphase nodes, cytokinesis nodes, and contractile rings (Akamatsu et al., 2014; Goss et al., 2014; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Airyscan fluorescence microscopy has ~140 nm resolution.
source: Here, we used the ~140 nm resolution of Airyscan super-resolution microscopy to measure the fluorescence intensity of small, single cytokinesis nodes marked with Blt1-mEGFP in live fission yeast cells early in mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is a known specification of the Airyscan technology.

claim: Airyscan microscopy resolves dim unitary cytokinesis nodes better than conventional confocal microscopy.
source: Large nodes stood out in the confocal images, but the higher background noise made it difficult to detect the dim cytokinesis nodes in broad bands.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison images in Figure 1.

claim: Contractile rings were brighter and narrower in Airyscan than confocal images.
source: Contractile rings were brighter and narrower in Airyscan than confocal images (Figure 1A, C, lower panels).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A, C.

claim: Fast Fourier transform analysis of images of cells with contractile rings showed that Airyscan retrieved higher frequencies and more extensively distributed information than confocal microscopy.
source: Fast Fourier transform analysis of images of cells with contractile rings showed that Airyscan retrieved higher frequencies and more extensively distributed information.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1B, D.

claim: Time-lapse imaging showed that cytokinesis nodes of all sizes, including single nodes, condensed into bigger and brighter nodes as they coalesced into a contractile ring during 10–12 min after separation of the SPBs.
source: Time-lapse imaging showed that cytokinesis nodes of all sizes, including single nodes, condensed into bigger and brighter nodes as they coalesced into a contractile ring during 10–12 min after separation of the SPBs as described for the brighter fraction of the population of nodes by confocal microscopy (Vavylonis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to Vavylonis et al., 2008.

claim: Neither the Airyscan nor confocal microscopy resolved cytokinesis nodes known to be present in contractile rings.
source: Neither the Airyscan nor confocal microscopy resolved cytokinesis nodes known to be present in contractile rings (Figure 1A, C, lower panels) by single-molecule localization microscopy (Laplante et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to Laplante et al., 2016.

claim: The mean fluorescence intensity of single cytokinesis nodes marked with Blt1-mEGFP is 2300 ± 900 AU.
source: For the sample of 231 single nodes, the Shapiro–Wilk W test calculated W = 0.9842, which does not reject the null hypothesis that the data are from a normal distribution (King and Eckersley, 2019; Royston, 1992). A descriptive statistical test also gave a Z score of 1.7, which also does not reject the null hypothesis that the data are from a normal distribution (Ghasemi and Zahediasl, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The distribution of fluorescence intensities of single cytokinesis nodes follows a normal distribution.
source: For the sample of 231 single nodes, the Shapiro–Wilk W test calculated W = 0.9842, which does not reject the null hypothesis that the data are from a normal distribution (King and Eckersley, 2019; Royston, 1992). A descriptive statistical test also gave a Z score of 1.7, which also does not reject the null hypothesis that the data are from a normal distribution (Ghasemi and Zahediasl, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with statistical tests supporting the claim.

claim: About 85% of the Blt1 in nodes is incorporated into contractile rings in wild-type cells.
source: The average total fluorescence intensities are 440,000 ± 95,000 AU in broad bands and 372,000 ± 111,000 AU in contractile rings. An unpaired t-test showed that these numbers are significantly different with p = 0.035. Thus, about 85% of the Blt1 in nodes is incorporated into contractile rings.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2E with statistical analysis.

claim: The average cell length of wee1-50 mutant cells after 4 hr at the restrictive temperature was about half the average length of wild-type cells.
source: After 4 hr at the restrictive temperature, the average cell length of wee1-50 mutant cells (8.0 ± 0.9 µm) was about half the average length of wild-type cells (14.2 ± 0.8 µm) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The diameter of wee1-50 mutant cells was the same as wild-type cells.
source: The diameter of wee1-50 mutant cells (3.8 ± 0.1 µm) was the same as wild-type cells (3.7 ± 0.1 µm).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: After 4–6 hr at 36°C, cdc25-22 mutant cells were 26.6 ± 5.7 µm long, twice the average length of wild-type cells.
source: After 4–6 hr at 36°C cells were 26.6 ± 5.7 µm long, twice the average length of wild-type cells but did not differ significantly in diameter (3.9 ± 0.1 µm) (Figure 3A) and had broader equatorial bands with more cytokinesis nodes (Vavylonis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: cdc25-22 mutant cells did not differ significantly in diameter from wild-type cells.
source: After 4–6 hr at 36°C cells were 26.6 ± 5.7 µm long, twice the average length of wild-type cells but did not differ significantly in diameter (3.9 ± 0.1 µm) (Figure 3A) and had broader equatorial bands with more cytokinesis nodes (Vavylonis et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Cells with deletion mutations of rga4 are shorter but have larger diameters than wild-type cells.
source: Cells with deletion mutations of rga4 are shorter (11.6 ± 0.7 µm) but have larger diameters (4.4 ± 0.2 µm) than wild-type cells (Das et al., 2007; Tatebe et al., 2008; Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citations.

claim: Deletion of rga2 does not change the cell length but decreases the cell diameter.
source: On the other hand, RhoGAP Rga2 localizes to growing cell tips and inactivates the Rho2 GTPase (Villar-Tajadura et al., 2008). Deletion of rga2 does not change the cell length but decreases the cell diameter (3.4 ± 0.2 µm) (Villar-Tajadura et al., 2008; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation.

claim: The distributions of Blt1 fluorescence intensities of single cytokinesis nodes were similar (around 2300 AU) in wild-type cells and all the experimental strains.
source: The distributions of Blt1 fluorescence intensities of single cytokinesis nodes were similar (around 2300 AU) in wild-type cells (Figure 2C) and all the experimental strains (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 2C and 3G.

claim: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes in the broad band were strongly correlated with cell volume with a slope of about 0.7 nodes per µm3 of volume.
source: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes in the broad band of our sample of 125 cells were strongly correlated with cell volume (Figure 3H) with a slope of about 0.7 nodes per µm3 of volume.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3H with linear regression analysis.

claim: Node numbers did not correlate with cell diameter.
source: Node numbers did not correlate with cell diameter (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The number of cytokinesis nodes in long, narrow rga2Δ cells (193 ± 39) was indistinguishable from wild-type cells (191 ± 41).
source: The number of cytokinesis nodes in long, narrow rga2Δ cells (193 ± 39) was indistinguishable from wild-type cells (191 ± 41) and aligned with the data from the other strains in plots of node number versus length and volume.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: The short, wide rga4Δ cells had fewer cytokinesis nodes (115 ± 40) than the wild-type and rga2Δ mutant cells with similar volumes.
source: On the other hand, the short, wide rga4Δ cells had fewer cytokinesis nodes (115 ± 40) than the wild-type and rga2Δ mutant cells with similar volumes (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The rga4Δ cells grew longer in 15 mM hydroxyurea for 4–6 hr and had the same number of nodes per volume as the other strains.
source: The rga4Δ cells grew longer in 15 mM hydroxyurea for 4–6 hr and had the same number of nodes per volume as the other strains (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The very large cdc25-22 mutant cells expanded the width of the broad band in proportion to the number of nodes.
source: The very large cdc25-22 mutant cells simply expanded the width of the broad band in proportion to the number of nodes, while the density of nodes and width of broad band both increased with their numbers in the other strains of freely cycling cells (Figure 3J, K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3J, K.

claim: The density of nodes and width of broad band both increased with their numbers in the strains of freely cycling cells other than cdc25-22.
source: The very large cdc25-22 mutant cells simply expanded the width of the broad band in proportion to the number of nodes, while the density of nodes and width of broad band both increased with their numbers in the other strains of freely cycling cells (Figure 3J, K).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3J, K.

claim: The five tested strains incorporated different fractions of the total Blt1-mEGFP in the cytokinesis nodes into their contractile rings.
source: The total Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in contractile rings was generally higher in large cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A), but did not scale cleanly with size because the five tested strains incorporated different fractions of the total Blt1-mEGFP in the cytokinesis nodes into their contractile rings: 85% in wild-type cells; 40–70% in cdc25-22, wee1-50, and rga2Δ mutant cells; and nearly 90% in rga4Δ mutant cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In cdc25-22 mutant cells, the total Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in cytokinesis nodes increased with cell volume but did not scale with cell size in their contractile rings.
source: In cdc25-22 mutant cells, the total Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in cytokinesis nodes increased with cell volume (Figure 3H) but did not scale with cell size in their contractile rings (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 3H and 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The largest cdc25-22 cells had as little as ~50% of the cytokinesis node Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in their contractile rings.
source: Therefore, the largest cdc25-22 cells had as little as ~50% of the cytokinesis node Blt1-mEGFP fluorescence in their contractile rings.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: cdc25-22 mutant cells recruited mEGFP-Myo2 to their contractile rings in proportion to their volumes.
source: In contrast, cdc25-22 mutant cells did recruit mEGFP-Myo2 to their contractile rings in proportion to their volumes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The local intensities of Pom1-mEGFP along the plasma membrane in the broad band did not vary significantly in the five strains with a fivefold range of sizes.
source: The local intensities of Pom1-mEGFP along the plasma membrane in the broad band did not vary significantly in the five strains with a fivefold range of sizes (Figure 4C) and 100–400 nodes (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The local Pom1 concentration did not vary like the Blt1-mCherry intensity along the plasma membrane in the middle focal plane of cells.
source: The local Pom1 concentration did not vary like the Blt1-mCherry intensity along the plasma membrane in the middle focal plane of these cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: During the G2/M phase transition of the cell cycle the local Pom1 concentration in the broad band does not control the variation in node number with cell size.
source: We conclude that during the G2/M phase transition of the cell cycle the local Pom1 concentration in the broad band does not control the variation in node number with cell size.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: The intensity of mEGFP-Pom1 in the broad band along the plasma membrane increased with the average concentration of Pom1 in the cells.
source: Artificially varying the total cellular concentration of Pom1 revealed the following dependencies as cells entered mitosis: the lengths of the cells (Figure 5C), the concentration of Pom1 along the plasma membrane in the broad band (Figure 5B), and the numbers of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) all increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1, while both the fluorescence of single nodes (Figure 5E) and the width of the broad band (Figure 5F) were constant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The length of cells undergoing the G2/M transition increased with the average concentration of Pom1 in the cells.
source: Artificially varying the total cellular concentration of Pom1 revealed the following dependencies as cells entered mitosis: the lengths of the cells (Figure 5C), the concentration of Pom1 along the plasma membrane in the broad band (Figure 5B), and the numbers of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) all increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1, while both the fluorescence of single nodes (Figure 5E) and the width of the broad band (Figure 5F) were constant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1.
source: Artificially varying the total cellular concentration of Pom1 revealed the following dependencies as cells entered mitosis: the lengths of the cells (Figure 5C), the concentration of Pom1 along the plasma membrane in the broad band (Figure 5B), and the numbers of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) all increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1, while both the fluorescence of single nodes (Figure 5E) and the width of the broad band (Figure 5F) were constant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The fluorescence of single nodes did not change with the cellular concentration of Pom1.
source: Artificially varying the total cellular concentration of Pom1 revealed the following dependencies as cells entered mitosis: the lengths of the cells (Figure 5C), the concentration of Pom1 along the plasma membrane in the broad band (Figure 5B), and the numbers of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) all increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1, while both the fluorescence of single nodes (Figure 5E) and the width of the broad band (Figure 5F) were constant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The width of the broad band of nodes did not change with the total Pom1 concentration.
source: Artificially varying the total cellular concentration of Pom1 revealed the following dependencies as cells entered mitosis: the lengths of the cells (Figure 5C), the concentration of Pom1 along the plasma membrane in the broad band (Figure 5B), and the numbers of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) all increased with the cellular concentration of Pom1, while both the fluorescence of single nodes (Figure 5E) and the width of the broad band (Figure 5F) were constant.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The ratio of the broad band width to the cell length decreased with the total cellular Pom1.
source: The ratio of the broad band width to the cell length decreased with the total cellular Pom1, indicating that Pom1 controls the width of the broad band (Figure 5H) as expected from previous work (Allard et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Pom1 controls the width of the broad band.
source: The ratio of the broad band width to the cell length decreased with the total cellular Pom1, indicating that Pom1 controls the width of the broad band (Figure 5H) as expected from previous work (Allard et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by citation to Allard et al., 2019.

claim: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes in cells expressing high Pom1 concentrations exceeded the numbers in cells of similar lengths and normal Pom1 concentrations.
source: The numbers of cytokinesis nodes in cells expressing high Pom1 concentrations exceeded the numbers in cells of similar lengths and normal Pom1 concentrations (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Cells expressing low concentrations of Pom1 were shorter when they divided with fewer cytokinesis nodes than cells with high Pom1 concentrations.
source: On the other hand, cells expressing low concentrations of Pom1 were shorter when they divided (Figure 5C) with fewer cytokinesis nodes (Figure 5G) than cells with high Pom1 concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 5C and 5G.

claim: Artificially increasing the total cell concentration of Cdr2 reduced cell length at the time of division.
source: Artificially increasing the total cell concentration of Cdr2 (Figure 6) reduced cell length at the time of division (Figure 6B) but did not change the width of the broad band of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 6C), so the broad band occupied a larger fraction of the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Artificially increasing the total cell concentration of Cdr2 did not change the width of the broad band of cytokinesis nodes.
source: Artificially increasing the total cell concentration of Cdr2 (Figure 6) reduced cell length at the time of division (Figure 6B) but did not change the width of the broad band of cytokinesis nodes (Figure 6C), so the broad band occupied a larger fraction of the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The number of cytokinesis nodes increased with the concentration of Cdr2.
source: On the other hand, the number of cytokinesis nodes increased with the concentration of Cdr2 (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The short cells expressing high Cdr2 concentrations had almost double the number of cytokinesis nodes in their slightly wider broad bands than cells of similar lengths with wild-type levels of Cdr2.
source: The short cells expressing high Cdr2 concentrations had almost double the number of cytokinesis nodes in their slightly wider broad bands than cells of similar lengths with wild-type levels of Cdr2 (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Longer cells expressing low concentrations of Cdr2 had numbers of cytokinesis nodes similar to cells of the same lengths with normal Cdr2 levels.
source: Longer cells expressing low concentrations of Cdr2 had numbers of cytokinesis nodes similar to cells of the same lengths in Figure 3I.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Cdr2 can drive cytokinesis node numbers above the basal level of about 190.
source: Therefore, Cdr2 can drive cytokinesis node numbers above the basal level of about 190.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data in Figure 6E.

claim: Cell size has a dominant influence in setting the number of nodes in wild-type cells.
source: Low SIN activity during interphase is a prerequisite for the assembly of type 1 interphase nodes (Pu et al., 2015), but cell size has a dominant influence in setting the number of nodes in wild-type cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data showing correlation between cell size and node number.

claim: As cells grow, the number of interphase nodes doubles as they mature into cytokinesis nodes.
source: Accordingly, as cells grow, the number of interphase nodes doubles as they mature into cytokinesis nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by previous literature.

claim: Only about half of each of the known node proteins assemble into nodes.
source: A limiting amount of an essential node protein might set the number of nodes, but only about half of each of the known node proteins assemble into nodes (Akamatsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citation to Akamatsu et al., 2017.

claim: Cells without either Cdr2 or Pom1 form cytokinesis nodes.
source: The presence of a basal number of cytokinesis nodes is expected, since cells without either Cdr2 or Pom1 form cytokinesis nodes Almonacid et al., 2009; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: Interactions of Pom1 with Cdr2 in type1 interphase nodes modulate the cell size, which in turn is the dominant determinant of the basal numbers of cytokinesis nodes in mitotic cells.
source: We propose that interactions of Pom1 with Cdr2 in type1 interphase nodes modulate the cell size, which in turn is the dominant determinant of the basal numbers of cytokinesis nodes in mitotic cells (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism based on the data.

claim: On top of the basal number of cytokinesis nodes, the concentrations of Cdr2 and Pom1 in mitotic cells can increase the number of cytokinesis nodes.
source: On top of this basal number of cytokinesis nodes, the concentrations of Cdr2 (Figure 6E) and Pom1 (Figure 5G) in mitotic cells can increase the number of cytokinesis nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figures 5G and 6E.

claim: Pom1 regulates interphase node localization by phosphorylating Cdr2, which reduces its oligomerization and membrane binding.
source: Pom1 regulates interphase node localization by phosphorylating Cdr2, which reduces its oligomerization and membrane binding (Bhatia et al., 2014; Rincon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: The gradient of Pom1 from the poles of the cell can restrict nodes to a broad band around the equator through its direct effect on Cdr2.
source: This direct effect of Pom1 on Cdr2 is one way the gradient of Pom1 from the poles of the cell can restrict nodes to a broad band around the equator (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: As cells grow, the overlap of the Pom1 gradient with Cdr2 in the middle of the cell decreases.
source: As cells grow, the overlap of the Pom1 gradient with Cdr2 in the middle of the cell decreases.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the known distributions of Pom1 and Cdr2.

claim: Pom1 regulates cell size at the time of division through a series of three inhibitory phosphorylation reactions: Pom1 phosphorylation inhibits the kinase activity of Cdr2; Cdr2 phosphorylates and inhibits the Wee1 kinase; Wee1 phosphorylates inhibitory sites on Cdk1.
source: In addition, Pom1 regulates cell size at the time of division through a series of three inhibitory phosphorylation reactions: Pom1 phosphorylation inhibits the kinase activity of Cdr2; Cdr2 phosphorylates and inhibits the Wee1 kinase; Wee1 phosphorylates inhibitory sites on Cdk1, the master mitotic kinase that promotes entry into mitosis (Allard et al., 2018; Breeding et al., 1998; Russell and Nurse, 1987).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: As cells grow, the influence of Pom1 on Cdr2 and Wee1 diminishes, contributing to the activation of Cdk1 and the transition into mitosis.
source: As cells grow, the influence of Pom1 on Cdr2 and Wee1 diminishes, contributing to the activation of Cdk1 and the transition into mitosis (Figure 7B; Allard et al., 2018, Allard et al., 2019; Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: Overexpression of Cdr2 might increase the number of cytokinesis nodes by mass action.
source: Based on these mechanisms, overexpression of Cdr2 might increase the number of cytokinesis nodes (Figures 6E and 7C) by mass action.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: Mass action may drive Cdr2 to inhibit enough Wee1 to promote premature mitosis, resulting in short daughter cells with more nodes packed more densely in a broad band of normal width.
source: In addition, mass action may drive Cdr2 to inhibit enough Wee1 to promote premature mitosis, resulting in short daughter cells (Figure 6B) with more nodes packed more densely in a broad band of normal width (Figures 6C, E, 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: High concentrations of Pom1 inhibit Cdr2, resulting in high Wee1 activity that inhibits Cdk1, delays the cell cycle, and allows cells to grow longer.
source: Based on the Pom1 to Cdk1 pathway, one expects high concentrations of Pom1 to inhibit the assembly of Cdr2 into nodes. However, inhibiting Cdr2 results in high Wee1 activity that inhibits Cdk1, delays the cell cycle, and allows cells to grow longer (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a proposed mechanism.

claim: The dominant effect of cell size on driving node formation produces more nodes when Pom1 is overexpressed.
source: The dominant effect of cell size on driving node formation produces more nodes (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed data.

claim: Wild-type cells form type 1 nodes around the daughter nuclei and use a gradient of Pom1 from the poles to confine these nodes to the equator throughout interphase.
source: Wild-type cells form type 1 nodes around the daughter nuclei and use a gradient of Pom1 from the poles to confine these nodes to the equator throughout interphase (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by previous literature.

claim: As cells elongate during interphase, the Pom1 concentration on the plasma membrane is low in a zone in the middle of the cell that widens in proportion to a wide range of cell sizes.
source: As cells elongate during interphase, three parallel events result in twofold longer cells with twice the number of nodes located in a twofold wider broad band ready for mitosis. First, the Pom1 concentration on the plasma membrane is low in a zone in the middle of the cell that widens in proportion to a wide range of cell sizes (Figures 3J, 4C,, 7B; Bhatia et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data and citations.

claim: Except in cdc25-22 mutant cells, the density and the total number of nodes marked with Blt1 or Cdr2 in the broad band increases with cell size in cells with or without Pom1.
source: Second, except in cdc25-22 mutant cells, the density (Figure 3K) and the total number of nodes marked with Blt1 (Figure 3H) or Cdr2 (Bhatia et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014) in this broad band increases with cell size in cells with or without Pom1 (Bhatia et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data and citations.

claim: The broad band widens in proportion to cell size.
source: Third, the broad band widens in proportion to cell size (Figure 3J).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 3J.

claim: One uncharacterized activity excludes nodes from one pole in the absence of Pom1.
source: Two additional factors contribute to limiting nodes to the equator. One is the uncharacterized activity that excludes nodes from one pole in the absence of Pom1 (Martin and Berthelot-Grosjean, 2009; Moseley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: Anillin Mid1 contributes to limiting nodes to the equator, given that nodes spread over the entire plasma membrane in mid1∆ cells.
source: The other is anillin, Mid1, given that nodes spread over the entire plasma membrane in mid1∆ cells (Saha and Pollard, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citation to Saha and Pollard, 2012.

claim: As arrested cdc25-22 cells grow at their tips, the extra nodes formed after the threshold time have room to spread out ever further from the edges of node broad band.
source: On the other hand, we hold the cdc25-22 mutant cells at the G2/M transition until releasing them into mitosis. As the arrested cells grow at their tips, the extra nodes formed after the threshold time have room to spread out ever further from the edges of node broad band.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed behavior of cdc25-22 cells.

claim: Overexpression of Cdr2 drives both node formation and premature cell division, while the natural level of Pom1-driven inhibition from the poles does not allow space for new nodes at the edges of the broad band, so the surface density of cytokinesis nodes is higher.
source: Overexpression of Cdr2 drives both node formation and premature cell division, while the natural level of Pom1-driven inhibition from the poles does not allow space for new nodes at the edges of the broad band, so the surface density of cytokinesis nodes is higher (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation for the observed data.

claim: Cells over expressing Pom1 have a higher density of nodes around their equators owing to more nodes in broad bands of normal widths.
source: Cells over expressing Pom1 also have a higher density of nodes around their equators owing to more nodes (Figure 5G) in broad bands of normal widths (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: Overexpression of Pom1 increases its concentration in the middle of cells and suppresses the spread of the broad band in spite of delayed mitosis increasing the length of these cells.
source: Like short wild-type interphase cells (Figure 7B), overexpression of Pom1 increases its concentration in the middle of cells (Figure 5B) and suppresses the spread of the broad band in spite of delayed mitosis increasing the length of these cells (Figures 5C and 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figures 5B, 5C, and 7A.

claim: The shape of the cell can influence the number of nodes.
source: The shape of the cell can also influence the number of nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a general observation.

claim: The large diameter rga4Δ mutant cells are normal in many ways (single node intensity, numbers, and densities of nodes for their lengths) but due to their large diameters, they are an outlier with fewer cytokinesis nodes than expected for cells with a given volume.
source: For example, the large diameter but short rga4Δ mutant cells lacking the RhoGAP Rga4 are normal in many ways (single node intensity, numbers, and densities of nodes for their lengths) but due to their large diameters, they are an outlier with fewer cytokinesis nodes than expected for cells with a given volume.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an observation from the data.

claim: The gradient of Pom1 from the cell tips is steeper in rga4Δ mutant cells than in wild-type cells.
source: In addition, the gradient of Pom1 from the cell tips is steeper in rga4Δ mutant cells than in wild-type cells and the Blt1-mCherry + Sad1-RFP fluorescence was spread more widely across the middle of rga4Δ mutant cells than in wild-type or other strains (Figure 4B, second and third panels from the top).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Most of the proteins comprising cytokinesis nodes during mitosis (Blt1, anillin Mid1, F-BAR Cdc15, IQGAP Rng2, and Myo2) are initially incorporated into contractile rings.
source: Most of the proteins comprising cytokinesis nodes during mitosis (Blt1, anillin Mid1, F-BAR Cdc15, IQGAP Rng2, and Myo2) are initially incorporated into contractile rings (Goss et al., 2014; Wu and Pollard, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: Myo2 is retained and concentrated in contractile rings along with newly arriving Myp2, while first Mid1 and then subsequently actin are lost in proportion to the declining circumference of the constricting contractile ring.
source: Thereafter, Myo2 is retained and concentrated along with newly arriving Myp2, while first Mid1 and then subsequently actin are lost in proportion to the declining circumference of the constricting contractile ring (Courtemanche et al., 2016; Malla et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations.

claim: The fraction of Blt1 in cytokinesis nodes incorporated into contractile rings varies: nearly 90% in rga4Δ mutant cells, 85% in wild-type cells, and 40–70% in cdc25-22, wee1-50, and rga2Δ mutant cells.
source: However, we report here that the fraction of Blt1 in cytokinesis nodes incorporated into contractile rings varies: nearly 90% in rga4Δ mutant cells, 85% in wild-type cells, and 40–70% in cdc25-22, wee1-50, and rga2Δ mutant cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data.

claim: In the longest cdc25-22 mutant cells, a much larger fraction of the Myo2 from the cytokinesis nodes was incorporated into the rings than Blt1.
source: In the case of the longest cdc25-22 mutant cells, a much larger fraction of the Myo2 from the cytokinesis nodes was incorporated into the rings than Blt1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Nodes observed in rings by single-molecule localization microscopy are likely to have different compositions than cytokinesis nodes.
source: In any case, this new observation indicates that nodes observed in rings by single-molecule localization microscopy (Laplante et al., 2016) are likely to have different compositions than cytokinesis nodes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.
